I don't think everyone who uses those phrases means them in the way you are interpreting them. For instance, people (including me) often say "a minimum wage job is intended to be an entry level, first job type position".

We don't mean the business necessarily intends it that way. Sometimes they may because they only intend to hire people who will stay with the company and proceed to higher positions. So they may really see it as an entry level stepping stone. More often, they assume turn over and everything else. They are simply paying what they need to pay to satisfy their business requirements.

What we really mean though is from the perspective of workers. Generally, if you are working at a minimum wage job after being in the work force, then you've done a shitty job managing your life. The reason you take those entry level, minimum wage jobs is to gain experience, have a resume, have good references from former managers. You are most likely young, or just getting on your own feet for whatever reasons. If it is not a stepping stone then you have set your goals pretty low.

No one, employer or employee, assumes a permanent minimum wage job is someone's career. The employer doesn't really care. They'll keep you on and pay you low wages if you do the required job. But most employees should have future steps in mind.
